The Holy Brook School
The government definition of extremism in its ‘Prevent Strategy’ is:
‘Vocal or active opposition to fundamental British values, including democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs; and/or calls for the death of members of our armed forces, whether in this country or overseas.’
At The Holy Brook School we work with children who, at times can display extreme forms of behaviour and who may express very outspoken thoughts and emotions. Sometimes these expressions represent genuine, although potentially disturbing, points of view born out of adverse experiences and at other times they are an attempt to anger, shock and/or hurt another individual.
It is important that staff do not confuse children expressing views that may not be an articulation of some inner rage or confusion with an indication of passive or active exposure to radical ideologies.
At HBS we promote British Values through Assemblies, Development Days and through our school curriculum. Please click here to read our summary of British Values.

The Holy Brook School
145 Ashampstead Road, Southcote, Reading, RG30 3LJ
admin@holybrook.reading.sch.uk
The Holy Brook School
Holy Brook Special School
Holy Brook Special School is a nurturing and inclusive community. It is a place where everyone is valued and all achievements are praised, celebrated and encouraged.
All children are supported, in a safe, happy and caring environment to:
At Holy Brook School, we envision a nurturing and inclusive environment where every one of our children thrives and we work in partnership with families. Our commitment is to recognize and celebrate the unique strengths, talents, and dreams of each student. We aim to provide a supportive and flexible curriculum that addresses individual learning barriers, sensory needs, and emotional well-being and that recognises our children as neuro divergent people.
We strive to create a safe, structured, and predictable environment that fosters trust, resilience, and self-advocacy. Through personalized education plans, multi-modal communication methods, and trauma-informed approaches, we empower our students to acquire communication, reading and mathematical knowledge that supports their future learning and helps them develop the essential life skills, social connections, and emotional literacy they need to thrive.
Our goal is to inspire a love for learning and creativity, encouraging our students to pursue their ambitions in diverse fields such as the arts, sciences, sports, and technology. By collaborating with families and the wider community, we ensure that our students are equipped with the tools and confidence to navigate their world and achieve their fullest potential.
Together, we build a future where every child at Holy Brook School feels valued, understood, and capable of making meaningful contributions to society and living a happy and fulfilling life.

On-Line Safety
At Holy Brook School we work hard to keep your child safe at all times. Please find below some useful information to help you to keep your child safe when they are on-line.
Does your child know the SMART rules?
The National On-Line Safety website provides really useful guides to help parents/carers with social media apps and platforms.
If you are worried about online hate, extremism or fake news this straight forward guide will help
Childnet has some really useful information, guidance and help including storybooks and other fun activities to help younger children learn more about e-safety. This is an excellent resource for parents of children aged 6-12. You can help your children with a quiz, learn to sing an online safety song or watch videos.
Visit www.thinkuknow.co.uk for more help and advice about E- Safety

School Meals
Our school meals are currently £2.66.
Meals are prepared, freshly, every day at our partner school, Manor Primary.
Every day your child will be offered a school meal that contains:
* 2 Portions of fruits and vegetables
* A dairy food item rich in calcium for strong bones & teeth
* Starch carbohydrates to provide energy
* A protein source to support the body's growth & repair
* If your child has an allergy, please let us know by completing the pupil information form.
If you have a child in Reception, Year 1 or 2 your child is entitled to enjoy a school meal every day for free (even on a school trip)
Free School Meals - Children in all year groups whose parents are in receipt of certain benefits will be entitled to a free school meal. If you believe that your child is entitled to a free school meal or you have any queries please contact Sarah in the school office for information on Tel: 0118 937 5489
